levels.title: Widest Road
levels.story: Fenn needs a fence between the sheep field and the vegetable patch, and a track beside it for the tractor. "Don't squeeze the fence next to the sheep," Fenn says. "Put it where the track is widest. Then a few strays won't spoil it."

everyday.scene: A town planner draws a new road between two neighbourhoods. A road squeezed against one side would cause trouble, so she places it halfway, with the most room on each side.
everyday.question: If many lines can separate two classes, which one should a computer choose?
everyday.answer: The one with the widest gap to the nearest examples on each side. That is the idea behind a support vector machine.

lessons.title: Many lines, one best
text: When two classes can be split by a straight line, many lines will do. A support vector machine picks the line with the widest margin: the biggest empty strip between the line and the closest points of both classes.
A wider margin leaves more room for a new point to land on the right side. On the number line, with A at 1, 2, 3 and B at 7, 8, 9, the best boundary is 5, with 2 to spare on each side.

terms.meaning: The empty strip between the boundary and the closest points.
The line, or point, that separates the classes.

references.title: scikit-learn user guide: Support Vector Machines

lessons.title: Only the edge points matter
text: The points that touch the edge of the margin are called support vectors. Here they are 3 and 7. If you moved the point at 9 further out, or deleted the point at 1, the best boundary would not move at all.
That makes the model compact: it only needs the support vectors to make predictions. The table shows each point's distance from the boundary at 5.

references.title: scikit-learn user guide: Support Vector Machines

lessons.title: Measuring the gap
text: In two dimensions a boundary is a line, such as 3x + 4y - 12 = 0. The distance from a point to that line is |3x + 4y - 12| divided by 5, where 5 is the square root of 3 squared plus 4 squared.

text.text: Real data often overlaps. A soft margin lets a few points sit inside the strip or on the wrong side, and a setting called C sets the trade-off between a wide road and keeping points on the correct side. A large C puts more weight on getting points right, and a small C puts more weight on a wide road.

references.title: scikit-learn user guide: Support Vector Machines

fieldNotes.title: Support vectors
fieldNotes.text: In a support vector machine, the samples that lie on the margin are called the support vectors.

fieldNotes.title: Memory friendly
fieldNotes.text: scikit-learn notes that support vector machines use a subset of the training points in the decision function, the support vectors, so they are also memory efficient.

summary: You placed a boundary halfway between two classes, found that only the edge points matter, and measured a margin with a distance formula.
Fenn raps a post at the exact midpoint. "Room for the sheep, room for the tractor."

mistake.title: Picking any line that separates the classes
mistake.text: Many lines work on the training points. The widest-margin line is the safest for new points, and only the points at its edge decide it.

levels.title: Bend the Map
levels.story: Fenn has a new puzzle. The prize pumpkins grow in the middle of the field, and the ordinary ones grow around the edges, on both sides. "No single fence line splits them," Fenn says. "Unless I bend the field."

everyday.scene: A flat map of the world cuts the Pacific Ocean in two halves. Roll it into a globe and the two halves join up. Some problems that look impossible in one view become easy in another.
everyday.question: What if no straight line can separate two classes?
everyday.answer: Add a new feature, such as the square of a value. In the new view the classes may be separable by a straight line. Kernels do this cleverly.

lessons.title: When a line fails
text: Sometimes no straight cut can split the classes. On a number line, class A sits at -1, 0 and 1, and class B sits at -4, -3, 3 and 4, on both sides of A. Wherever you cut, B ends up on both sides.
The fix is not a smarter cut but a different view. A new feature can lift the points so that a straight cut works.

lessons.title: Lift the points
text: Add a new feature by squaring each value. A becomes 1, 0 and 1. B becomes 16, 9, 9 and 16. Now one straight cut, at 5, splits them.

Going back to the original numbers, that cut at a squared value of 5 means the boundary sits at x = 2.236, the square root of 5, on each side. A straight line in the new view becomes a curved boundary in the old one.

references.title: scikit-learn user guide: Support Vector Machines

lessons.title: The kernel trick
text: Building new features can get huge. The kernel trick avoids that. A kernel is a function that gives the similarity two points would have in the lifted view, without ever building it. A support vector machine only needs those similarities.

One kernel is (x . z) squared. For x = (1, 2) and z = (3, 1), the dot product is 5, so the kernel is 25. Another popular choice is the RBF kernel, e to the power of minus gamma times the distance squared, which gives 1 for identical points and fades to 0 far away.

text.text: The squared-dot-product kernel gives exactly the same number as lifting each point to three features (x1 squared, root 2 times x1 times x2, x2 squared) and taking the ordinary dot product. For the points above, both ways give 25.

references.title: scikit-learn user guide: Support Vector Machines

fieldNotes.title: Non-linear boundaries
fieldNotes.text: Support vector machines can perform non-linear classification using the kernel trick, which implicitly maps inputs into a higher-dimensional feature space.

fieldNotes.title: Common kernels
fieldNotes.text: scikit-learn's SVM classes support several kernels, including linear, polynomial, RBF and sigmoid, and you can also supply your own.

summary: You saw that a straight cut can fail, lifted the points with a squared feature so that it worked, and met the kernel trick that saves building the new features.
Fenn paints a circle round the pumpkins. "Straight in the new view. Round in the field."

mistake.title: Thinking a straight-line model can only draw straight boundaries
mistake.text: In a lifted view the boundary can be a straight line and still look curved in the original view.
